key_insight: A hybrid human-AI pipeline uses LLMs to translate expert and stakeholder knowledge into formal preference structures, which are then fed into an optimization model to prioritize health post upgrades and maximize population coverage under resource constraints.
problem_solved: How to prioritize scarce health-post upgrade investments in Ethiopia to maximize coverage and equity while systematically incorporating diverse expert and stakeholder preferences that are typically qualitative and hard to formalize.
method: Elicit qualitative preferences from local experts and stakeholders and use LLMs to parse, standardize, and convert those narratives into quantitative preference signals (weights, constraints, or scoring rules).
Integrate the encoded preferences into a facility-location optimization (e.g., budget-constrained coverage maximization with equity considerations) to generate ranked upgrade plans.
Iterative human-in-the-loop validation with the Ethiopian Public Health Institute and Ministry of Health to refine preference encoding and assess robustness/sensitivity of plans.
impact: Demonstrates a practical workflow for combining LLM-driven knowledge extraction with classical optimization to make transparent, stakeholder-aligned decisions in resource-constrained public health settings—useful for AI practitioners building human-centered, deployable decision systems.

paper_title: Health Facility Location in Ethiopia: Leveraging LLMs to Integrate Expert Knowledge into Algorithmic Planning
